memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "They made the lampstand of pure gold. They hammered out its base and shaft, and made its flowerlike cups, buds and blossoms of one piece with them." - Exod 37:17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
No joints. No welding. No pieces fitted together. The entire lampstand — base, shaft, branches, cups shaped like almond blossoms — was hammered out of a single block of gold.

That took extraordinary patience. Every hammer blow shaped the gold without breaking it, over what must have been weeks of work. One careless strike and it was ruined.

The design says something about unity. Jesus prayed that His people would be one, as He and the Father are one (John 17:21). Not many separate lamps standing near each other, but one stand with many branches — like the vine and its branches, drawing life from the same source (John 15:5).

But there is something else here. Beauty in gold is produced by hammering. There is no other way to shape it.

Many of us are in a season that feels like blows we did not ask for. Scripture does not romanticise suffering, and we should never tell someone their pain is simply God's craftsmanship. But it does say that God is at work in it — that suffering produces perseverance, character and hope (Rom 5:3-4), and that our present troubles are achieving an eternal glory (2 Cor 4:17).

The Craftsman knows exactly how hard to strike.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where do you feel you are being shaped by difficulty right now?
2. Do you see yourself as separate from other believers, or joined to them?
3. What helps you trust God's hand when the shaping hurts?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You know exactly what You are forming in me. Help me trust Your hands when the shaping is painful. Amen.
